subject: Hosted API latency SLO phasing & evidence capture for FinTrust
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@fintrust.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API latency SLO phasing & evidence capture for FinTrust

Elena —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. To move the SLA addendum forward we want to propose a pragmatic, measurable approach for the hosted API latency commitments that balances FinTrust's real-time needs with our capacity/observability constraints. High level proposal:

- Initial commitment (first 60 days): p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 360ms measured on a rolling 1-hour window (UTC).
- Stabilized commitment (after month 3): p50 <= 30ms, p95 <= 250ms measured on a rolling 1-hour window with 5-minute sampling cadence for alerting.
- Bursts & transient carveouts: automated short-burst carveout for up to 10 minutes per incident; sustained degradation will follow our remediation playbook and credits (outlined in the addendum).

We captured a small traffic sample and synthetic-benchmark evidence (attached) to show the delivery path and the expected tail behavior under your typical request mix. Can you confirm whether the 1-hour rolling window aligns with your reporting needs, or do you require a different measurement epoch (e.g., daily aggregate or 5-minute rolling for contractual p95)?

Next steps I suggest:
1) You confirm measurement epoch preference and any regional constraints.
2) We finalize SLA addendum and route for DocuSign.
3) Redwood provides an evidence package and ops playbook (attached) for your audit team.

Open to a short call tomorrow if that helps.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
(415) 555-0127

Attachments: redwood_latency-evidence-sept.xlsx (spreadsheet), fintrust-traffic-sample.json (json sample), sla-addendum-draft.pdf (pdf)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@fintrust.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: FinTrust SRE <sre@fintrust.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency SLO phasing & evidence capture for FinTrust

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear proposal. A few requests from our side:

- Measurement window: for contractual p95 we need a daily-rolling window for billing and penalty triggers; for operational alerting we prefer 5-minute rolling windows. In practice we'd expect Redwood to publish both (daily for SLA calculation, 5-minute for ops).
- The initial p95 of 360ms looks acceptable as a phased target, but can we add a clause that accelerates the stabilized commitment (250ms) to 45 days if traffic mix matches the provided sample and error budget is under 0.5%?
- Evidence: can you produce percentile breakdowns by request type (short prompt vs long prompt) and regional split (us-east vs us-west)? Our SRE will validate.

If you can update the addendum with the daily rolling contractual window + operational 5-minute window and the accelerated ramp clause we can aim to sign next week.

—Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Reliability, FinTrust
elena@fintrust.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@fintrust.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency SLO phasing & evidence capture for FinTrust

Elena —

Thanks — this is helpful and reasonable. Quick responses to each point: 

1) Measurement windows: we can provide both. Contractual p95 will be computed on a daily rolling window for billing/penalty triggers; operational metrics and alerts will use a 5-minute rolling window with a 1-hour aggregation retained for reporting. We'll detail the exact calculation (inclusive/exclusive of warmup and prefix-cache hits) in the addendum appendix.

2) Accelerated ramp clause: agreed in principle. Proposed language: "If observed traffic mix and 45-day rolling error budget (errors/user-visible failures) remain below 0.5% and observed p95 on daily window is <= 300ms for 14 consecutive days, Redwood will accelerate stabilized p95 target to 250ms." Happy to refine wording with your legal team.

3) Evidence breakdown: attached sheet includes percentile by short/long prompt buckets (we used your sample thresholds) and a regional split. If your SRE wants additional traces we'll share sanitized request traces (no PII) under NDA.

I've attached an updated SLA addendum draft (pdf) and a small evidence workbook. If that looks good I'll loop in Legal and route for DocuSign.

Callout: we currently rely on a rolling 1-hour measurement to smooth transient noise for billing; your ask for a daily contractual window is fine, we'll include both explicitly and document the canonical window for invoice calculation.

Would you like to sign the addendum with the accelerated ramp clause or keep it discretionary?

Thanks,
Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
(415) 555-0127

Team —

Good work. A couple of internal asks before we send the finalized addendum: 

- Legal: ensure the acceleration clause has a clear objective metric (we should avoid vague language like "in principle") — Marcus, work with Legal to add the exact threshold sentence you suggested.
- Finance: pre-approve provisional credits language for short sustained degradations (>30m) so Sales can commit to timelines. Aditya, can you get a quick nod from Finance on credit caps?
- Ops: confirm we can instrument both 5-minute and daily windows in our public telemetry; Kimberly, please validate that the reporting exports include the daily contractual calc and the 5-minute ops stream.

I'll review the addendum doc now and BG it if it's aligned. If Legal and Finance can turn quickly we should be able to sign within 5 business days.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Lauren/Marcus/Aditya —

Checked the instrumentation plan: we can publish both 5-minute and daily-series. A couple operational notes:

- The daily contractual p95 will be computed by first removing maintenance windows and applying the documented short-burst carveout rules; the final numbers will be signed off by our metrics team.
- For the accelerated ramp we need FinTrust to provide an admin contact that will confirm the traffic sample match; we can accept a validated CSV from their SRE.

I'll prepare a tidy appendix for the addendum showing calculation steps and a sample export file format. Sending that to Marcus within the hour.

Kimberly Park
